headline: Social contracts are the agreements—explicit and implicit—that make living together possible
universal_truth: Society runs on agreements; most aren't written down but are understood and expected
fun_facts: Philosophers like Hobbes, Locke, and Rousseau developed social contract theory
Most social agreements are implicit—never stated but understood
Breaking unwritten rules often carries social rather than legal consequences
discussion_questions: What unwritten rules govern your interactions?
When have you seen social contracts broken?
How do implicit agreements differ from explicit ones?

hook.script: Most rules aren't laws. They're agreements—spoken or unspoken—about how we'll treat each other. Don't cut in line. Return borrowed things. Keep promises. These social contracts enable cooperation without enforcement.

cliff.script: Why do people follow rules that aren't enforced by law?

options.text: Social contracts enable cooperation—breaking them invites social consequences and erodes trust; we follow unwritten rules because life works better when people can rely on each other
options.response: Yes. Social rules run on reputation and relationship. Break them and others stop cooperating with you. Keep them and you're trusted, included, helped. Society is mutual rule-following.
Pressure is the enforcement mechanism, but the rules themselves enable the trust that makes society work...

fact1.title: Implicit Agreements
fact1.script: Most social rules aren't discussed—they're understood. You learned them growing up. The fact that they're implicit makes them powerful. You follow rules you never consciously agreed to.

fact2.title: Trust Foundation
fact2.script: Social contracts build trust. When everyone follows the rules, you can rely on others. This trust is society's foundation. Widespread rule-breaking collapses cooperation.

fact3.title: Renegotiating Rules
fact3.script: Social contracts can change. What was expected in one era might not be in another. As society evolves, implicit agreements get questioned and renegotiated. This is healthy.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Society runs on agreements. Most aren't written down but are understood and expected. Honor the contracts that make cooperation possible.

outro.script: That's Day 336. Tomorrow, we'll explore how people trade. Until then, notice the unwritten rules you follow.

growTrack.title: Social Contract Awareness - What Rules Do You Follow?
growTrack.activity: What unwritten rules govern your daily life? Make a list of social expectations you follow that aren't laws. Which do you think are valuable? Which might need renegotiating?
